The glass dropped heavily to the table empty and his hand hovered around it, even while his eyes and mind were focused elsewhere, glassy. The taste of the cheap whiskey burned on the back of his tongue and down his throat. He sits there now in the dim glow of the old monitor that illuminates the dust motes floating around the old room. Perhaps, maybe, a change of scene would spark some activity, some notion, some thread from which to continue. He could write. Damn, could he write, if only he would write.

His body jerks to motion, but once upright, sways like a peaceful wave, steadying itself against the nearby wall as the motes dance joyfully in and out of the light. With pen and paper in hand, he unsteadily moves toward the other room. After flicking the switch, the room reveals itself: a bit cleaner than barely habitable. Maybe the bed, maybe the single seating table? Or the floor. Controlling the planned collapse, he displaces a few bottles with his stretched out legs and props himself up on his elbows. The papers, decorated with a few ink doodles in the corner, shuffle in a slight cross breeze from the crack under his door and the crack in his single window. He grasps the pen dominantly, powerfully moving it against the paper so as to strike inspiration from it, but when the tip scrawls weakly across the first line, the ink means nothing, and in petulant frustration, he flings the useless thing far from him. After some length of stupefied delay, he understands this hated thing’s necessity and slowly drags his numb body after it. Propping himself up against the nearest cupboards, he eyes his own fear and hatred, examining the simple mechanized ball point, the mess of ink around the tip, the clip, broken off by incessant gnawing, the dirty smudges and flaws along the sides. His eyes wandered, distracted by a not yet empty bottle of cheap gin in that one cupboard that he could never get to close. His infantile hands dropped the abandoned pen, seeking inspiration from this new toy, this new hope. He closed his eyes with a mix of pain and joy as he finished consulting his abusive muse, begrudgingly releasing her from his grasp when he realized her short tolerance of him was worn through. Now fading in and out, his hazy attention returns to the sheets of paper, strewn by his struggle to reach the pen. They lay there, stark white and for the most part, unblemished, accusing him, accusing this apartment, unable to achieve their own full potential, held back by this creature, now sinking to the floor, now closing his eyes, peaceful finally.
